new_assertions.title: shortest-route phase equals the distinguished final residual bit
new_assertions.body: For each of the two shortest 5x4 routes, the observed route phase bit equals the P0 membership bit of residual token 197700 in that route's represented final exact residual state: route A gives 0=0 and route B gives 1=1.
new_assertions.scope: exactly the two shortest 5x4 routes represented in the packet
new_assertions.note: No extension to other routes or a coordinate-free mask identity is asserted.

new_assertions.title: required target phase difference equals residual-bit difference
new_assertions.body: In every satisfying scalar assignment of the residual-bit-refined shortest witness, the two refined target phase values differ by XOR 1, and the two represented target residual-membership bits also differ by XOR 1.

new_assertions.title: the coarse target merge identifies values forced to differ
new_assertions.body: The current target quotient merge identifies the two final states even though every satisfying refinement-level scalar assignment requires their target phase values to differ; imposing one shared target phase value is therefore exactly the additional equality that makes the shortest constraint system inconsistent.

new_assertions.title: a local endpoint residual coordinate reproduces route phase
new_assertions.body: On the represented two-route shortest-witness family, after refining the target by residual-token-197700 membership, route phase is an endpoint function of that refined residual bit; no route-history variable is needed to distinguish phase 0 from phase 1 for these two routes.
